agree.reason: The offer is clear and the vacancy arithmetic is persuasive, but a landlord who still remembers the 2024 late payments and has a coffee chain interested gets no reason to trust the reliability claim and no concrete push to accept.

honest.reason: The figures check out: about $5,740 in year five, two vacant months at $11,300 against a $6,600 yearly gap, and more than two years of on-time rent. But 'ready to sign now' goes slightly beyond anything the brief establishes.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the year-five rent and compares the cost of vacancy with the rent gap, both to good effect, but it never gives the per-square-foot rate of $5,100 (about $26.30, below the $28 unit that is still sitting empty), which would make the offer look strongest.

right_comparison.reason: The 14-month vacancy at $28 a square foot is a solid market benchmark, but the coffee-chain alternative is left unexamined: a new tenant's buildout, lost months and lease-up risk are never set against keeping this tenant.

qualification.reason: The only timing condition is 'well before August', which gives no specific response date (such as June 1) and no consequence if it is missed.

objections.reason: The landlord's main grievance, the two late payments, is passed over instead of being explained (a one-time cooler failure) or answered with a remedy such as automatic payment, and the coffee chain is met only with a soft appeal.

fit.reason: It is a short, polite letter of roughly 260 words, well under the 300-word limit, with bullet points that are easy to scan, though the name fields are still bracketed placeholders.
